drivingQuestion: Is 'upon the wood' indispensable, or may the burnt offering lie directly on the altar?

segments.he: בָּעֵי חִזְקִיָּה: אֵבָרִין שֶׁסִּידְרָן וְסִידֵּר עֲלֵיהֶן אֶת הַמַּעֲרָכָה, מַהוּ? ״עַל הָעֵצִים״ אָמַר רַחְמָנָא דַּוְקָא עַל הָעֵצִים, אוֹ דִלְמָא כֵּיוָן דִּכְתִיב קְרָא אַחֲרִינָא: ״אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכַל הָאֵשׁ אֶת הָעֹלָה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״, אִי בָּעֵי הָכִי עָבֵיד, אִי בָּעֵי הָכִי עָבֵיד? תֵּיקוּ.
segments.en: «Ḥizkiyya raises a dilemma:» With regard to the «limbs» of the burnt offering «that» a priest «arranged» on the altar «and arranged the arrangement» of wood on the altar «on top of them, what is» the halakha? Do we say that «the Merciful One states:» “And Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall lay the pieces and the head, and the fat, in order «upon the wood» that is on the fire upon the altar” (Leviticus 1:8), teaching that they must be placed «specifically upon the wood? Or perhaps, since it is written» in «another verse: “That which the fire will consume of the burnt offering on the altar”» (Leviticus 6:3), indicating that the burnt offering may be arranged directly on the altar, «if» the priest «desires» to arrange the limbs in «this» manner he may «do» so, «and if» he «desires» to arrange them in «that» manner he may also «do» so. The Gemara comments: No answer was found, and the dilemma «shall stand» unresolved.
